concept.learning_outcome: Learner can name the four EI abilities, distinguish evidenced core from oversold popular version, and apply reappraisal the next time they notice a strong feeling.
concept.central_question: Is emotional intelligence a real, useful skill or a buzzword -- and either way, what can you do with it?
major_principles: Understanding people (including yourself) is a distinct, learnable skill.
EI has a real definition narrower and better-evidenced than its popular version.
Response to a feeling changes the outcome more than the feeling itself.
Naming a feeling accurately precedes managing it.
concept.historical_or_lost_knowledge_angle: Thorndike 1920 social intelligence -> Gardner 1983 interpersonal/intrapersonal intelligence -> Salovey & Mayer 1990 formal EI definition.
concept.current_use_angle: Reappraisal vs. suppression (Gross 1998); RULER framework (Yale Center for Emotional Intelligence).
concept.transfer_the_principle_summary: Naming and understanding a signal before reacting to it produces a better decision than reacting on the raw signal -- applied to personal, family, communication, work/leadership, and money decisions, with an explicit limit on where the analogy stops applying.
visual_needs: reappraisal-vs-suppression comparison graphic (factual, sourced from Gross 1998, not decorative)
